newsitem.title: UK: UK life and pension sales rise 41 pct in third qtr.
newsitem.headline: UK life and pension sales rise 41 pct in third qtr.

text.p: An upswing in sales of life assurance and pensions in the UK is gathering pace, with total new business rising more than 40 percent in the third quarter, a key insurance industry association said on Friday.
Sales of new life and pensions business in the third quarter were 4.5 billion stg, 41 percent higher than over the same period in 1995, said the Association of British Insurers (ABI).
It was the fourth quarter in a row to see a year on year increase in sales, after an upturn became apparent during the latter part of 1995.
"These impressive figures are welcome news for insurers and the economy," said the ABI's general director Mark Boleat.

"They indicate that the uppturn in the sales of life and pension products which became evident towards the end of last year is gathering pace, and show growing consumer confidence and appreciation in the value of long-term savings."
Premium income for new life assurance business rose by 48 percent to 3.3 billion stg, while premium income for new individual pensions increased by 24 percent to 1.2 billion.
